questiontext.text:
Exercise

Each graph below shows a function defined on the interval drawn. Which of these functions are invertible? Select every graph that shows an invertible function.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
A function has an inverse exactly when it is one-to-one: each output comes from only one input, so the function takes each value in its range precisely once. On a graph, use the horizontal line test: if some horizontal line meets the graph more than once, two different inputs give the same output and the function is not invertible.

In this variant the graphs show (a) \(y = {@version[1]@}\), (b) \(y = {@version[2]@}\), (c) \(y = {@version[3]@}\) and (d) \(y = {@version[4]@}\).

Graphs (\({@lbls[pc[1]]@}\)) and (\({@lbls[pc[2]]@}\)) are always increasing or always decreasing, so every horizontal line meets each of them at most once: these functions are invertible. Graphs (\({@lbls[pw[1]]@}\)) and (\({@lbls[pw[2]]@}\)) each meet some horizontal line two or more times, so they are not invertible.

questiondescription.text: Grade 11 Functions (inverse functions; overlaps with 16.8 Inverse of Polynomials). Identifies invertible functions from their graphs with the horizontal line test. Adapted from the STACK sample multiselqnalpha.

node.description: Only invertible graphs selected, but one missed (half marks); otherwise a non-invertible graph was selected

truefeedback.text: Every graph you selected is invertible, but there is another invertible function in the list. Apply the horizontal line test to each graph you did not select.

falsefeedback.text: At least one graph you selected is not invertible: {@setdifference(setify(ans1),setify(corr1))@}. Some horizontal line meets such a graph more than once, so two different inputs give the same output. A function is invertible only if every horizontal line meets its graph at most once.

qtest.description: One invertible plus one non-invertible graph
Only one of the two invertible graphs (half marks)
